::: {#exr-spread}
#### Applying a function to a list

`(apply f L)` applies the function `f` to the elements of the list `L` as its arguments,
so `(apply + (list 2 7 6))` is the same as `(+ 2 7 6)`, which returns 15.

1. Guess what `(apply max (list 3 9 2))` returns.
2. Use `apply`, `max` and `min` to define `(spread L)`,
   which returns the largest element of a nonempty list of numbers minus its smallest element.
3. Guess what `(spread (list 4 -1 7 2))` returns.

:::
